title: Carried-failure follow-ups: one record-id predicate, a doc sentence that misstates the 409 remedy, and a header for a newest evaluation with no failures
outcome:
Lows and Notes from the Claude reviewer of w-f7620f648ea8, round 3 (delegation-1eb1dad5-1fc2-4c58-a321-d091e25f46cb).

(1) is_acceptance_record_id (src/acceptance_evaluation.rs) is a copy of is_engram_record_id (src/engram_host_adapter.rs:3100). Keep one predicate, so the submission check and the adapter cannot drift apart.

(2) docs/features/engram-host-adapter.md describes the same 409 two ways: the newer sentence names the two remedies (unpin the task's mode, or admit independent_session in the policy), while an older one says "request an independent evaluation". Make them agree.

(3) Note: `newest` is built whenever the evaluation's hash differs from the carried id. If Engram ever shows a newest evaluation with no failing verdicts, the header would say "did not pass 0". Either set newest only when it has failing verdicts, or word the header from the count.

(4) Note: when nothing is carried, the new pre-pass renders the full brief twice. A guard on task.carried_failure.is_some() avoids that.
acceptance: One record-id predicate serves both the acceptance submission and the host adapter; the two docs sentences about the same_session 409 name the same remedies; a newest evaluation with no failing verdicts is not described as a failing one; a test covers the last point.
